definition: Human-Robot Collaboration is the study of collaborative processes in human and robot agents work together to achieve shared goals.
details: Many new applications for robots require them to work alongside people as capable members of human-robot teams. These include robots for homes, hospitals, and offices, space exploration and manufacturing. Human-Robot Collaboration (HRC) is an interdisciplinary research area comprising classical robotics, human-computer interaction, artificial intelligence, process design, layout planning, ergonomics, cognitive sciences, and psychology. Industrial applications of human-robot collaboration involve Collaborative Robots, or cobots, that physically interact with humans in a shared workspace to complete tasks such as collaborative manipulation or object handovers.

explainer.lead: Human–robot collaboration studies how human and robot agents work together toward shared goals. It matters because many new applications, from homes to hospitals to manufacturing, require robots to act as capable teammates alongside people.

tiers.eli5: It's about people and robots working as a team on the same job, like a robot handing tools to a worker.
tiers.practitioner: It is an interdisciplinary area spanning classical robotics, human-computer interaction, AI, process design, layout planning, ergonomics, cognitive sciences, and psychology. A pitfall is that shared workspaces demand safety and coordination, not just capable robots.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as the study of collaborative processes in which human and robot agents work together to achieve shared goals; it is interdisciplinary and covers fields including robotics, HCI, AI, process design, ergonomics, and psychology, with industrial applications.

explainer.example: In a factory, a robot and a human worker share a task, with the robot's behavior designed around safety and coordination for the shared goal.
